headline: 13-Year-Old Kenyan Plants 7,600 Trees, Demands Youth Climate Action
meta_description: Baraka Moruri, 13, has planted over 7,600 trees in Kenya and is calling for world leaders to include young people in climate decisions.
summary_short: A Kenyan teenager has planted more than 7,600 trees in four years and is urging global leaders to give youth a seat at the climate action table.
body:
Baraka Moruri was 9 when he planted his first tree. Four years later, the Kenyan teenager has mobilized his family, friends, and local organizations to plant over 7,600 trees across Nairobi—from schoolyards to national forests—and his ambition is far larger: he wants to plant one million trees before turning 18. But Baraka's real mission extends beyond trees. At 13, he is demanding that world leaders and policymakers stop sidelining young people in climate action, arguing that children have crucial ideas and energy to contribute to solving the crisis that will ultimately define their lives.

Baraka's passion took root after watching a documentary about Nobel Peace laureate Wangari Maathai during a school assignment. The Kenyan environmentalist's legacy inspired him, and the devastating 2026 floods that killed 110 people and displaced 34,700 crystallized his sense of urgency. He now speaks directly about what he observes: shifting seasons that confuse farmers, droughts and heat waves that make concentration impossible at school, and the overlapping climate shocks—from floods to fires—that leave one in four children in East and Southern Africa exposed to multiple hazards simultaneously.

Yet Baraka operates at a stark disadvantage. Less than 1% of international climate finance reaches youth- and children-led projects, experts say, despite children bearing the heaviest burden of climate change. His mother funds most of his work herself, relying on donations from a handful of organizations. In November 2023, Baraka mobilized 700 people for a climate walk that yielded 2,000 newly planted trees—a testament to his organizing power. He aims to speak at COP31 in Türkiye this November, carrying a message that older generations need to hear: young people are not waiting for permission to lead.
